findings.subject: TERM_AGE, TERM_CONFLICT, TERM_INVOLVEMENT, TERM_RECENT_RESEARCH
findings.detail: LimeSurvey has no terminate action. The build inverts every terminate rule into the main group's relevance and nests the disposition messages into one end screen. Message text recovered for 4 of 4 screenout destinations. Assertions must test 'main group suppressed' plus 'end screen shows this text', never a page named after the disposition.

findings.subject: TERM_AGE, TERM_CONFLICT, TERM_INVOLVEMENT, TERM_RECENT_RESEARCH
findings.detail: these 4 dispositions share identical end-screen text ('Thank you for your interest. You do not qualify for this survey.'), so Agent 4 sees the same words whichever rule fired. An end-text assertion proves a screenout occurred, not which one. To distinguish them the QRE must give each disposition its own wording.

findings.subject: Q5->Q6
findings.detail: 6 of 6 carried-forward options have a different code at each end. 'Primary-care physician' is SQ001 at Q5 and A001 at Q6; 'Specialist' is SQ002 at Q5 and A002 at Q6. LimeSurvey matches a carry-forward filter by code rather than by text, so the labels reading correctly at both ends does not mean the filter works. Worth confirming against a hand-built survey before treating as a defect

content.note: Derived from the emitted .lss, not from a self-reported build manifest. The .lss is what LimeSurvey actually imports, so it is stronger evidence than a manifest of intent.
